stop_conditions: At least two independent sources (e.g., Redis telemetry and metrics/traces) confirm or refute cache-degradation on inventory-service.
A root cause or dominant contributor is identified and no unresolved strong conflict remains between sources.
Inventory-service cache hit/miss and TTL root cause is established, or an alternative Redis-related cause is confirmed.
Observation window closes without reproducing the suspected cache-degradation signal, requiring a new hypothesis set.
initial_hypotheses: Inventory-service cache effectiveness degraded: catalog TTL misconfiguration (negative ttl) or runaway MOVING SQL (products ORDER BY id LIMIT) is bypassing or evicting cache, causing repeated DB calls.

Redis is a shared chokepoint used by gateway, order-service, inventory-service, payment-service, notification-service; degradation here could elevate latency across the critical path independent of inventory.
Observed HTTP latency (order-service p99 ~75ms, gateway p99 ~97ms) reflects fan-out to inventory-service and downstream cache/DB contention rather than an error-driven failure.
Order-service checkout path (POST /checkout -> payment-service /charge) may bottleneck on inventory-service cache-miss retries, amplifying tail latency.

arguments.hypothesis: No incident: observed latencies are within normal bounds and the apparent "inventory db_qps collapse" (baseline 109 -> current 6.4) is an artifact of non-comparable baselines, not a live degradation. Product catalog reads (products ORDER BY id LIMIT) run at ~6 calls/20s and ~0.10 ms mean exec time, Redis shows a high cumulative miss ratio but TTL=-2 is a cumulative snapshot flag, not proof of misconfiguration. Root cause UNKNOWN / no active failure.
arguments.reasoning_summary: All services return 0% errors and low latency (gateway p99 97ms, order-service p99 75ms). Traces show the checkout critical path entirely in gateway/order/payment with no error spans and no repeated calls; inventory-service does not even appear in that trace's critical path. pg_stat shows inventory-service connections idle in ClientRead with catalog queries ~0.10ms mean. S1's suspect (cache degradation) is not corroborated by trace or HTTP metrics; db_qps delta is a baseline mismatch.
arguments.next_evidence_needed: Confirm whether inventory db_qps baseline (109/s vs 7.7 req/s total traffic) is a stale/control-plane-inclusive baseline; if nothing further corroborates cache degradation, decide UNKNOWN/no-incident.

arguments.hypothesis: No active failure: all services healthy with 0% errors and low latency; the "inventory-service cache degradation" signal is unsupported. The apparent db_qps drop is a baseline artifact (baseline ~109/s vs total observed traffic ~7.7 req/s) and the products ORDER BY id LIMIT query has ~0.10 ms mean exec time with 6 calls/20s delta. Redis cumulative miss ratio (197k misses vs 47k hits) is a cumulative, control-plane-inclusive counter, not current cache degradation. Root cause UNKNOWN / no incident within window.
arguments.root_cause: Within the observed ~20s window every service reports 0.00% errors and modest latency (gateway p99 ~66–98 ms, order-service p99 ~43–75 ms, inventory-service p99 ~9–13 ms). The checkout trace's critical path runs gateway -> order-service -> payment-service/charge with no error spans and no repeated calls; inventory-service does not appear on that path, so its cache cannot explain the tail. Database evidence shows all connections idle in ClientRead (no lock/IO waits), the catalog read SELECT id,name,price,stock FROM products ORDER BY id LIMIT $1 executes in ~0.10 ms mean over 3.7k cumulative calls with only 6 new calls in the snapshot, and a separate pg_sleep query with 1202 ms mean is a control/chaos artifact, not application traffic. The triage's "db_qps collapse" (baseline 109/s -> current 6.4/s) is inconsistent with the measured request rate (~7.7 rps total across services), indicating a non-comparable/stale baseline rather than a live degradation. Redis counters (47017 hits / 197288 misses) are explicitly cumulative and include control-plane traffic, and catalog_ttl = -2 is a snapshot flag, not evidence of a TTL misconfiguration. With no error, no trace-level degradation, and no DB or Redis saturation, the correct determination is UNKNOWN / no reproducible active failure in this window.
llm_findings: All services report 0.00% error and low latency across two snapshots; no error spans in the sampled checkout trace.
Checkout critical path is gateway -> order-service -> payment-service; inventory-service is absent, so inventory cache cannot drive the observed tail.
Postgres shows only ClientRead idle sessions; the catalog ORDER BY id LIMIT read averages ~0.10 ms with 6 new calls in the window — no MOVING SQL pressure.
inventory-service db_qps 'collapse' (109 -> 6.4) is inconsistent with ~7.7 rps total traffic: a baseline comparability artifact, not degradation.
Redis 47017 hits / 197288 misses is explicitly cumulative and includes control-plane traffic; catalog_ttl=-2 is a snapshot flag, not proof of TTL misconfiguration.
pg_sleep with 1202 ms mean exec time is a control/chaos artifact and should be excluded from service SLO interpretation.
arguments.recommended_fix: No code change. Operational follow-ups: (1) re-baseline the inventory-service db_qps metric — the 109/s baseline is inconsistent with ~7.7 rps observed traffic, so alarms on it are unreliable; (2) compute Redis hit/miss from snapshot deltas per time window and exclude control-plane keys, to avoid false cache-degradation alarms; (3) verify catalog TTL configuration explicitly (read the inventory-service cache TTL config) before treating catalog_ttl=-2 as a misconfiguration; (4) isolate the pg_sleep(1202 ms mean) workload as a chaos/control probe and exclude it from service SLO dashboards.
arguments.reasoning_summary: Two independent source classes refute the cache-degradation hypothesis: (1) HTTP metrics + traces show 0% errors, no error spans, no repeated calls, and a checkout critical path that never enters inventory-service; (2) Postgres activity shows every connection idle in ClientRead with the catalog read at ~0.10 ms mean and only 6 new calls, i.e., no query pressure. The triage's only positive signals (db_qps delta -102, Redis miss-heavy counters, catalog_ttl -2) are all explained by baseline mismatch and cumulative/snapshot semantics explicitly flagged in the evidence notes. No conflicting observation remains that indicates a live degradation, so the incident is UNKNOWN rather than a specific failure mode.

deterministic_signals.explanation: Catalog reads run ~6 calls/20s at ~0.10 ms mean with all DB connections idle in ClientRead (no IO/lock waits); the checkout trace critical path skips inventory-service and has no error spans or repeated calls; inventory HTTP p99 is ~9-13 ms with 0% errors. Redis miss-heavy counters are cumulative and control-plane-inclusive, and catalog_ttl=-2 is a snapshot flag, so neither proves cache degradation.

remaining_uncertainty: Whether inventory-service's catalog TTL is genuinely misconfigured cannot be verified from a single cumulative snapshot; requires reading cache config and two Redis snapshots over time.
The db_qps baseline provenance (109/s) is unknown — it may mix control-plane or historical traffic; without metric lineage this cannot be fully excluded.
Observation window is short (~20s) at low traffic (~7.7 rps); a rarer cache-miss-driven tail could exist outside this window.
